headline: Singapore Launches 100+ Refill Stations for Eco-Friendly Cleaners at 30% Discount
meta_description: Household product manufacturer Lam Soon is opening over 100 refill stations across Singapore to tackle low recycling rates and offer cleaning products at 30% c…
summary_short: Singapore is getting over 100 refill stations for cleaning products, offering 30% discounts while tackling the city's stalled recycling rates.
body:
Singapore's recycling rate has plateaued at just 11%—well short of the government's 2030 target of 70%. Now, household product manufacturer Lam Soon is taking direct action by deploying over 100 refill stations across the city, offering their Bio-Home line of biodegradable cleaners at a significant discount. By eliminating packaging altogether, the company can pass savings of 30% to customers, with prices starting at around SGD$4.80 per liter. Consumers bring their own reusable containers and refill them at the vending machine-style stations, removing the need for single-use bottles before they ever become waste.

The initiative represents what experts call an "upstream" solution—addressing the problem at its source in the supply chain rather than waiting for waste to pile up for recycling. Lam Soon invested $1 million into the tech startup Ecoworks, which designed the refill infrastructure and is now rolling out installations across the city. Already, the stations have appeared at two university campuses and a community center, with plans to expand to over 100 locations in total.

"Ecoworks has identified what is required for reuse to scale—convenient, standardized infrastructure in every neighborhood," the company noted. This approach recognizes a hard truth: with recycling stuck in place despite decades of awareness campaigns, changing how products are sold and consumed may be the key to moving the needle. By making sustainability cheaper and more convenient than the wasteful alternative, Lam Soon is testing whether Singapore can finally break through its recycling plateau.
quick_facts: Over 100 refill stations deploying across Singapore
30% price discount on Bio-Home cleaning products
Lam Soon invested $1 million into startup Ecoworks
Singapore's recycling rate stuck at 11%, aiming for 70% by 2030
Prices start at SGD$4.80 per liter for refilled products
